Definition: from G3844 and the base of G3795; a side-dish (the receptacle):--platter.
BiblicalUsage: Paropsis is a platter, a side-dish, the vessel set beside the table. Jesus uses it in Matthew 23:25 and 23:26, where the Pharisees make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess, and He tells them to cleanse first that which is within.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the platter teaches what the cup taught: God washes from the inside out, and a clean outside on a dirty dish is a lie the whole table can see.
